pue.boundary: Bloom supplies and services on-site generation. It does not operate the matched Nebius or Oracle data-center IT-energy perimeter.
pue.basis: PUE is matched total data-center energy divided by IT-equipment energy. The 250 MW guaranteed / 328 MW installed generation ratio is a contract-design ratio, not PUE, availability, utilization or reserve margin. Customer-site operational PUE is not disclosed, so no modeled PUE range is invented.

model.revenue_period: Nebius Capacity Agreement: three phases with 10-year supply term each
model.revenue_scope: Up to $2.6B aggregate monthly capacity-service fees over the disclosed supply terms. This is a contractual upper bound, not recognized quarterly revenue, product revenue, facility compute revenue or a financing commitment.
model.capacity_time_basis: 2,500 guaranteed generation MW-years, calculated as approximately 250 aggregate guaranteed generation MW times 10 years. Phase start dates and phase-specific capacity are not public, so the output is an aggregate contract upper bound rather than a period-average active-capacity result.

formulas.customer_site_PUE: sum(matched total facility energy) / sum(matched IT-equipment energy), IT-energy weighted across sites and periods

structured_deals.status: Executed 2026-05-14; three phases; deployment expected during 2026
structured_deals.economic_effect: Nebius buys guaranteed capacity and associated electricity while Bloom installs, operates and maintains approximately 328 MW installed generation supporting approximately 250 MW guaranteed generation. Aggregate monthly service fees are up to $2.6B over three 10-year supply phases, implying a $1.04M upper bound per guaranteed generation MW-year before undisclosed fuel, escalation, commencement and performance adjustments.

structured_deals.status: $1.7B project investment announced 2026-07-16 for the Nebius deployment
structured_deals.economic_effect: IDF leads development, Oaktree supplies minority equity, Morgan Stanley is tax-equity investor and placement agent, and MUFG supplies senior debt. The structure funds project assets outside Bloom's general balance sheet, while Bloom remains economically exposed to delivery, operations, warranties and fee commencement.

structured_deals.status: Framework expanded to $25B on 2026-06-30; current Bloom Fund JV exposure reported at 2026-06-30
structured_deals.economic_effect: The $25B amount is a five-year financing framework, not recognized Bloom revenue or RPO. Bloom reported $77.3M of Fund JV commitments and $68.8M maximum loss exposure at June 30; project creditors have no recourse to Bloom's general credit and Bloom provides no guarantees beyond committed contributions.

structured_deals.status: Up to 2.8 GW master arrangement; 1.2 GW described as contracted and deploying into next year
structured_deals.economic_effect: Bloom issued a warrant for 3,531,073 shares at $113.28, cashlessly exercised on 2026-05-01. Aggregate fair value of issued shares including inducement was $324.4M and is recorded as customer consideration reducing revenue as Oracle Energy Servers are delivered; cumulative reduction was $17.9M at June 30. No public contract price or IT-load denominator supports a $/MW result.

structured_deals.status: Project Jupiter announced 2026-04-27; up to 2.45 GW installed fuel-cell generation
structured_deals.economic_effect: Oracle says the fuel cells will fully power the campus and Oracle bears energy costs. The disclosed 2.45 GW is generation capacity, not facility or IT load, and cannot establish PUE or operator revenue per effective IT MW.

Bloom claims its 800 V DC architecture can reduce non-compute capex by $3.6B, or 27%, and five-year TCO by $5.5B, or 9%, versus AC for an illustrative 1 GW compute site. This is an issuer model with project-specific assumptions, not audited realized savings or PUE evidence.

findings: Bloom's Q2 revenue reached $1.065B, but 87.8% was product revenue and one non-related customer represented 73%, approximately $777.7M. The filing warns that the reported customer can be a project-finance affiliate rather than the end user, making delivery and financing timing central to the growth profile.

The Nebius contract provides the cleanest supplier power metric: up to $2.6B over approximately 250 guaranteed generation MW for 10 years, or $1.04M per guaranteed generation MW-year. The corresponding installed-capacity upper bound is $0.793M per installed generation MW-year.
The 250 MW guaranteed / 328 MW installed ratio is 76.2%. It is a contractual generation ratio only; it is not availability, utilization, reserve factor or PUE.

Third-party project finance supports deployment scale while limiting Bloom's current Fund JV balance-sheet exposure. Bloom reported $68.8M maximum loss and $77.3M commitments at June 30, while creditors have no recourse to Bloom's general credit beyond committed contributions.

The Brookfield $25B framework, Oracle 2.8 GW master arrangement and Project Jupiter 2.45 GW generation plan are strategic capacity or financing headlines, not recognized revenue, RPO or period-average active IT MW.

Bloom's liquidity is stronger than a pure cash-burn story: first-half operating cash flow was $300M and cash was $2.667B versus $2.475B of recourse debt. Customer concentration, product-delivery timing, warranty performance and financing affiliate execution remain the main read-through risks.

Supplier PUE is not applicable and customer operational PUE is not disclosed. No operator revenue-per-effective-utilized-IT-MW range is published because the matched IT-load, physical utilization and compute-revenue perimeter are absent.
